question: What will France's provisional year-on-year CPI inflation be for November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Bottom-up: y/y_Nov ≈ 3.4 + (m/m Nov26 − m/m Nov25 [-0.2 definitive, incl. energy rebound]). Pump prices Nov MTD vs Oct avg: diesel −6.6% (2.370→2.214), SP95-E10 −5% (2.155→2.048), still falling mid-month after strategic-reserve destocking and Brent <$90; petroleum contribution ≈ −0.25 to −0.35pp, partly offset by regulated gas +6.6% (≈+0.1pp). Energy y/y falls from 24.1% to ~20-21%, taking ~0.2-0.3pp off headline → central ~3.1-3.2. Trading Economics model forecast 3.8% (likely doesn't incorporate fuel drop) and weight uncertainty pull median up slightly. No human market found (Kalshi CPI contracts are US).

- Oct 2026 CPI y/y 3.4% (prov 30 Oct and def 13 Nov), m/m +0.4%; energy +24.1% y/y; services +2.6-2.7%; food +1.2%; manuf −0.2% (INSEE 9107965; CB News 2026-11-16).
- Nov 2025 base: definitive m/m −0.2% (prov −0.1%); services −0.5% m/m (transport −5.4% seasonal); manuf −0.1%; energy rebounded (petroleum up); y/y 0.9% (INSEE 8672064; Boursorama 2025-12-12).
- Since 1 Nov 2026 France destocking 10m barrels of strategic reserves sold at historical cost; diesel down 18-20c/L: 2.37 end-Oct → 2.17 on 10 Nov; measure lasts to Mar/Apr 2027 (lautomobiliste.fr 2026-11-10; selectra 2026-11-01).
- Monthly average pump prices (mon-carburant.com, MTD as of ~16 Nov): diesel Oct 2.370 → Nov 2.214 (−6.6%); SP95-E10 2.155 → 2.048 (−5.0%); SP98 2.266 → 2.165; GPL slightly up. SP95-E10 1.991 on 16 Nov, still falling.
- Brent briefly below $90 on 10 Nov 2026.
- Regulated gas benchmark +6.6% on 1 Nov (182.88→194.90 €/MWh); +5.8% due 1 Dec (outside window). Heating oil included in price controls from 1 Nov.
- Approx CPI weights (author recollection, not verified): petroleum products ~4%, gas ~1.1-1.2%, electricity ~2.8%, services ~50%.
- Trading Economics model forecast for Nov prelim y/y: 3.8% (tradingeconomics.com).
- Flash vs definitive differences recently 0-0.1pp (Sep 3.0→3.1; Oct 3.4→3.4).
- Status quo: unchanged 3.4%. Resolves off INSEE provisional headline IPC ensemble y/y (not IPCH, not m/m), published 27 Nov 2026.
- Event window: November 2026 reference month (1-30 Nov); as of 16 Nov ~53% elapsed.
- Searched but not found: economists' consensus for France Nov flash, exact 2026 CPI weights, any France-CPI prediction market (none found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi).

Nov 2026 pump prices fell sharply after strategic diesel-stock release: Nov 1-16 avg diesel 2.214 vs Oct 2.370 (-6.6%), E10 2.048 vs 2.155 (-5%), diesel still falling mid-month -> petroleum ~-6 to -7% m/m (~-0.3pp), partly offset by regulated gas +6.6% (~+0.08pp). Fuel full-month averages likely −6 to −8% vs Oct after strategic diesel stock release (effective weight ~5% given +38% y/y) → ~−0.35pp; regulated gas +6.6% → ~+0.1pp; ex-energy seasonal Nov decline ~−0.3pp as in 2025. m/m ≈ −0.5 → y/y ≈ 3.1. Upside: services pass-through, late-month fuel rebound; downside: continued fuel slide. No prediction market found.
calls.reconciliation: Factual: Nov 2025 base m/m — Run 3 used provisional −0.1, Runs 1-2 definitive −0.2; y/y uses the definitive index, so −0.2 governs, shifting Run 3's arithmetic down ~0.1. Judgment: petroleum effective weight and full-month fuel decline — mid-month spot prices below MTD averages imply a full-month drop larger than MTD, so I take ~−0.35pp. Trading Economics 3.8 discounted as a model not reflecting the fuel drop. Median ~3.1, close to Run 2, with ~12% mass at ≤2.9. No web access this run.
